title: Pharmacology of BCL2 Inhibitors in hematological diseases (PhaB2i)
summary:
In various blood cancer diseases, the mechanisms for the degradation of damaged cells, i.e. programmed cell death (apoptosis), are impaired. mong other things,  occurs through an upregulation of inhibitors of apoptosis, such as B-cell lymphoma-2 proteins (abbreviated BCL2). The drug class of BCL2 inhibitors (abbreviated BCL2i) blocks the mechanisms of blood cancer cells, allowing apoptosis to be initiated. In addition to the desired effect on blood cancer cells, side effects in the form of a deficiency of the hematopoietic system can occur. Some patients react so strongly to the substance that planned dosing intervals must be altered or the dosage reduced. In the European Union, Venetoclax is currently approved as a representative of BCL2i for the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (abbreviated CLL) and acute myeloid leukemia (abbreviated AML). Caution is already required during the initial dosing of the drug due to its potent effect.
Caution is already required when dosing the active ingredient. Due to its potent effect, there may be a strong breakdown of blood cancer cells. The average age at diagnosis for both diseases is 69 years. People who develop CLL or AML often have altered organ functions compared to young adults. This study aims to investigate whether changes in organ function or other risk factors lead to enhanced effects of BCL2 inhibitors. The purpose of the survey and blood sample analysis is to determine the level of the active ingredient in the blood and to correlate this with patients' reports of side effects or changes in habits.
